gen-irish-grover-gf-hind-siliguri: Hind Siliguri reads with a steady gray hum, its rounds left slightly open like a cracked bangle. Irish Grover is the one with the sturdy, tall-lowercase swagger, while the body keeps every line at a single weight.
gen-irish-grover-gf-hind-vadodara: Fun is the first thing Irish Grover says, with its gently swelling and thinning strokes. Hind Vadodara follows in a plain sans with spacious gaps in its rounds and big open e and a, so a long passage flows without any pressure swells slowing the eye.
gen-irish-grover-gf-karla: Irish Grover has tall lowercase that makes words look sturdy, and its mild thick-thin shifts smooth the reading pace. Karla's stocky, tall middle band holds up the plain sans text beneath it.
gen-irish-grover-gf-kedebideri: Tall lowercase that looks sturdy and large, with hairline thinning only modest at the curves, is what defines Irish Grover. Kedebideri sits beneath in plain sans, its rounded letters tall and inviting.
gen-irish-grover-gf-khula: Irish Grover stands up tall and sturdy, its horizontals lighter than the verticals but never threadlike. If the size needs adjusting, nudge Khula, whose curves hold their mouths open.
gen-irish-grover-gf-krub: Irish Grover cuts its letters like stencils, with mildly varied bar widths and open-throated a, c, e and s. Krub brings a pronounced x-height and unfinished curves, and that gap between them is the pair's best feature.
gen-irish-grover-gf-kufam: Irish Grover swings between robust downstrokes and slender turns, giving its sturdy tall lowercase some friendly movement. Kufam runs a single neon-tube track through every stroke, so its open-curved sans-serif text glides along without a bump.
gen-irish-grover-gf-lexend: Irish Grover tapers its joins modestly without letting them vanish, and the result looks fun and organic. Lexend keeps bowls and stems at one weight, with open jaws on its curves, so sans-serif text moves along easily.
gen-irish-grover-gf-lexend-deca: Lexend Deca reads as a plain, unshaded line, with small-looking capitals beside big lowercase and terminals that stop short of curling. Irish Grover adds the modest weight shifts within each stroke, giving the pair some friendly life.
gen-irish-grover-gf-liter: Modern is the mood Liter carries, with stroke contrast of exactly none and wide mouths on its round forms. Liter reads in plain sans with great vertical presence, while Irish Grover holds the top with a restrained difference between stem and connecting stroke.
